title: Review months of coding agent logs to see how you work
summary: A developer analyzed seven months of logs from five coding agents. He reports $28,335 spent, 201,473 agent actions, about 15 actions per message he typed, and almost nothing overnight.
agent_role: Coding agents did the hands-on work in short supervised runs. The author interrupted them about 2,047 times and wrote scripts to analyze the session logs.
outcome: Author reports 9,350 commits across 145 repositories. Spending rose 7.4 times once he started running agents side by side, but only 0.7% of agent actions happened overnight.
what_they_did: Chirag Aggarwal ran Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents for seven months. He then analyzed their saved session logs by hour and by day. He also tracked how often he stopped a run, how many actions each agent took per message, and how often he used his 130 installed add-on skills.
how_it_went: He reports the agents averaged about 15 actions before he stepped in. Spending tracked his workday: $176 a day on weekdays and $67 on weekends. Only 52 skill runs happened across all his transcripts.
worth_knowing: He keeps runs short on purpose. Past about 15 actions, he says, he is no longer reviewing the work, just accepting it.
prompt: Look through my saved coding agent session logs in [log folder]. Write a script that counts tool calls by hour of day and by day of week. Also count my messages per session, how often I interrupted a run, and the average number of tool calls per message I sent. Count how often each installed skill was actually used. Show the script before running it. Then summarize the findings in a short report with simple charts.

curation.rationale: A data-rich look back at seven months of the author's own coding-agent logs, with real numbers on cost, interruptions and timing. It reflects on how he used agents rather than showing a specific task, so it rates as thin but genuine.
